related_questions.question: What to know before traveling to Italy?

text_blocks.snippet: Before traveling to Italy, ensure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay and check visa requirements. Research transportation options, including trains, buses, and potentially rental cars, and validate tickets when required. Learn basic Italian phrases and be aware of local customs, like cheek kissing greetings. Pack comfortable shoes for walking, appropriate clothing for religious sites, and essentials like adapters and chargers. Be prepared for potential delays on public transportation, and consider downloading offline maps and translations.
snippet_highlighted_words: ensure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay and check visa requirements

list.title: Passport and Visa:
list.snippet: US citizens can stay in Italy for up to 90 days without a visa for tourism or business. Ensure your passport is valid for six months beyond your travel dates.

list.title: Transportation:
list.snippet: Italy has a good public transportation system, especially trains. Consider downloading the Trenitalia app for easy train travel. Validate your train or bus tickets to avoid fines.

list.title: Currency:
list.snippet: The currency in Italy is the Euro.

list.title: Language:
list.snippet: While English is spoken in tourist areas, learning basic Italian phrases will enhance your experience, especially in smaller towns.

list.title: Health:
list.snippet: Be up-to-date on routine vaccinations. Consider vaccinations for Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B if at high risk. Pack any necessary prescription medications, as they are not always readily available.

list.title: Safety:
list.snippet: Stay alert in tourist areas and be aware of your surroundings. Review the Country Security Report for Italy.

list.title: Packing:
list.snippet: Comfortable walking shoes are essential for exploring Italian cities. Pack layers, as the weather can vary. Bring adapters and chargers for your electronics.

list.title: Dining:
list.snippet: Cappuccino is traditionally a morning drink in Italy. Be aware of restaurant hours, as they may close between lunch and dinner.

list.title: Customs:
list.snippet: Be prepared for cheek kisses as a greeting, and dress modestly when visiting religious sites.
